module_title: Advanced Economic, Niche Demographic, and Multi-Tiered Schemes
introduction: This advanced matrix explores multi-ministerial implementations, strategic credit lines, and specialized security frameworks rolled out between 2016 and recent fiscal periods. These schemes feature counter-intuitive nodal ministries or rigorous mathematical parameters.

core_concepts.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME). Jointly supported by Ministry of Skill Development & Ministry of Finance.
- Launch Date: September 17, 2023
- Core Objective: End-to-end holistic support to traditional artisans and craftspeople (covering 18 trades like carpenters, blacksmiths, potters) including skill upgrading, toolkit incentives, collateral-free concessional credit, and digital transaction branding.

core_concepts.title: PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
- Launch Date: June 1, 2020
- Core Objective: A micro-credit facility introduced during the COVID-19 pandemic to offer affordable working capital loans (starting at ₹10,000) to street vendors to resume their livelihoods in urban, peri-urban, and rural areas.

core_concepts.title: Agnipath Scheme
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Defence
- Launch Date: June 14, 2022
- Core Objective: A transformative recruitment model for the Armed Forces where selected youth (termed 'Agniveers') enroll for a short-term contractual duration of four years, aimed at fostering a leaner, younger profile for the military.

core_concepts.title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
- Launch Date: February 18, 2016
- Core Objective: A uniform crop insurance scheme protecting farmers against yield losses due to natural calamities. It mandates uniform, highly discounted premium rates: **1.5% for Rabi crops, 2.0% for Kharif crops, and 5.0% for commercial/horticultural crops**.

core_concepts.title: Stand-Up India Scheme
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Finance
- Launch Date: April 5, 2016
- Core Objective: To promote entrepreneurship at the grassroots level by mandating every bank branch to extend bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower, and at least one Woman borrower, specifically for setting up greenfield enterprises.

important_entities.name: PM SVANidhi Ministry Counter-Intuition
important_entities.key_fact: Credit Scheme Under an Urban Ministry
important_entities.significance: Because PM SVANidhi deals directly with financial loans and credit capital lines, intuition leans toward selecting the Ministry of Finance or MSME. However, because its targeted demographic belongs strictly to urban ecosystems, **MoHUA** is the sole Nodal Ministry.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Advanced UPSC statements will try to claim that the Ministry of Skill Development is the sole operator because the scheme trains traditional artisans. In reality, it is a tri-ministerial architecture where the **Ministry of MSME** serves as the primary anchor/nodal office.

Stand-Up India credit lines are strictly limited to **Greenfield projects** (the first-time venture of the borrower in that specific sector). Options stating it can be used for diversifying or expanding an existing manufacturing plant are false.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Rabi crops (winter) have the lowest volatility/premium at 1.5%. Monsoon-dependent Kharif scales up to 2.0%, and commercial/cash horticultural crops sit at the maximum cap of 5.0%.

exam_strategy_tips: When facing multi-statement analysis questions, look closely at specific numerical thresholds like loan metrics (e.g., Stand-Up India's range of **₹10 Lakh to ₹1 Crore**) or premium percentages in PMFBY. Examiners frequently modify these values to generate incorrect options.
